1	# Conventions
2	
3	Where a file goes, what it is called and what it may import. These are rules, not taste: each
4	is here because its absence produced a defect, and changing any of them needs an ADR exactly
5	as any other rule under `spec/design/` does.
6	
7	What the system *is* — its contexts, containers and flows — is described by
8	[`architecture.md`](architecture.md). How it is run, tested and developed is stated by
9	[`CLAUDE.md`](../../CLAUDE.md).
10	
11	## Layers
12	
13	Layering is strict and one-directional:
14	
15	```
16	app/contexts/<name>/ or app/platform/
17	  routers/   HTTP only: binding path/query/body, status codes, dependency injection
18	     ↓
19	  services/  business rules, transactions, the whole data-loading pipeline
20	     ↓
21	  models/    declarative SQLAlchemy mappings
22	  schemas/   Pydantic request and response contracts (never reused as ORM models)
23	```
24	
25	**The layer is a directory inside a slice, never above one** (§ Backend — where a file goes).
26	Layering itself is unchanged by that; only the depth at which the directories are found.
27	
28	**`services/`, `models/` and `schemas/` may not import `fastapi` or `starlette`.** Every module
29	in those packages says so in its docstring. This is what keeps business rules testable without
30	HTTP and reusable from an Alembic migration and a CLI script. Checked by
31	`tests/fitness/test_layering.py`.
32	
33	**Dependencies point one way**: `routers` → `services` → `models`/`schemas`. A service
34	importing a router, or a model importing a service, is a defect.
35	
36	A service **never names a status code**. It raises a domain exception; the router translates it,
37	explicitly, in a `match` block. `app/core/errors.py` registers three *framework* handlers and
38	knows nothing about the domain. The sentence an operator reads belongs beside the endpoint that
39	produced it, not in a shared table one edit away from telling somebody the wrong column to
40	correct. The worked example is `_not_found` in `app/contexts/guestbook/routers/guestbook_entries.py`.
41	
42	**A rule about a field's value whose refusal carries a code of its own is judged in `services/`,
43	and `schemas/` holds no part of it.** A refusal about the request as a whole, a `PATCH` that sets
44	no field, is decided beside the endpoint before the service is called ([`api.md`](api.md)
45	§ Shapes, `GuestbookEntryUpdate`). A constraint or a validator in a schema answers before the
46	route runs, with FastAPI's list of `{loc, msg, type}` and no code. So a schema holds only a bound
47	whose refusal needs no code of its own. The guestbook's `BR-01` bounds are that case, and the
48	guestbook is the worked example of that case, not of every bound. Where [`api.md`](api.md) gives
49	a refusal a code, the request shapes carry the field with no bound, so a shape built from a
50	refused value is still a valid shape. **Holding no part of the rule means importing none of it:**
51	the service's judgement imports the rule's parts — the bound beside the model and the shared
52	kernel's `normalize` and `length` (`app/platform/schemas/text.py`) — and `schemas/` imports
53	neither. The service judges the value before any write and raises one domain exception per
54	verdict, and the router translates each one into its coded refusal, as above. A to-do task's
55	text is such a rule: normalize, then empty, then one line, then measure. The user decided it in
56	`CR-2609-823a` (`Q-17`) in these words: "The service checks it, with a coded reason." The user
57	drew both edges of the rule in the same change (`Q-21`): "Refusing an edit that changes nothing
58	is decided at the endpoint, as the guestbook does; only rules about a field's value go to the
59	service", and "The request formats import no part of the text rule; the service does."
60	
61	## Backend — where a file goes
62	
63	**The outermost cut is the bounded context; the layer is a directory inside it.** A new domain
64	concept adds **one file per layer, named after the concept**, under the context that owns it —
65	`app/contexts/guestbook/models/guestbook_entry.py`,
66	`app/contexts/guestbook/schemas/guestbook_entries.py`,
67	`app/contexts/guestbook/services/guestbook_entries.py`,
68	`app/contexts/guestbook/routers/guestbook_entries.py`. Never `utils.py`, `helpers.py` or
69	`common.py`: a name that describes nothing attracts everything.
70	
71	The reason the context is outermost is **ownership**, not taste. `.github/CODEOWNERS` matches
72	paths, so a tree cut by layer can hand somebody every context's `services/` — a quarter of each —
73	and can never hand them one context. A path that holds one context and nothing else is what
74	makes a context something a person or a team can be given.
75	
76	```
77	app/
78	  main.py            the composition root: middleware, the router, the assets, the SPA shell
79	  api.py             the one place the `/api` prefix is applied; one line per context
80	  contexts/<name>/   a bounded context and everything of it: models schemas services routers
81	  platform/          the supporting technical slice — HTTP with no domain rules in it
82	  core/  db/         infrastructure used by Platform and by every context alike
83	```
84	
85	- **`app/contexts/<name>/__init__.py`** — the context's **public API**. Another context may
86	  import `app.contexts.<name>` and nothing below it; `tests/fitness/test_context_boundaries.py`
87	  refuses the rest. Importing it imports the context's models, which is what registers its
88	  tables on the shared `Base`.
89	- **`app/api.py`** — the aggregate, and **the `/api` prefix is applied there and nowhere else**,
90	  so a router registered anywhere else lands outside `/api` and is swallowed by the SPA
91	  catch-all. It is the **composition root**: the one module allowed to reach a context's router
92	  module, because a neighbouring context has business with a `GuestbookEntry` and none whatever
93	  with the function that binds it to a URL. One line per context, listed rather than
94	  discovered — so the registration can be checked in both directions.
95	- **`app/contexts/<name>/routers/`** — HTTP binding only, one module per resource, each
96	  exposing `router`. `guestbook` is this template's worked example through every layer: copy
97	  it, and when your own context replaces it, delete it. The to-do list (`todo_list`) is a second
98	  domain context and is not an example.
99	- **`app/contexts/<name>/services/`** — business rules. Owns the session and the transaction
100	  boundary.
101	- **`app/contexts/<name>/models/` + `alembic/versions/`** — one class per file, `Base` from
102	  `app/db/base.py`. Every schema change is a revision; `create_all()` is never called. Domain
103	  constants the whole application must agree on live beside the model they describe
104	  (`AUTHOR_MAX_LENGTH` in `app/contexts/guestbook/models/guestbook_entry.py`). See
105	  [`data-model.md`](data-model.md).
106	- **`app/contexts/<name>/schemas/`** — Pydantic request and response models, the file name
107	  plural per resource, the classes suffixed (`GuestbookEntryRead`, `GuestbookEntryCreate`).
108	  Read and write shapes are separate classes even when they are identical today. See
109	  [`api.md`](api.md).
110	- **`app/platform/`** — the technical slice: liveness, the health shape, the refusal envelope
111	  and the text rule. **Two files here are not named after a resource, and that is a rule rather
112	  than an exception to one.** `app/platform/schemas/refusals.py` carries the refusal envelope
113	  with a code, which is a fact about EVERY refusal this API makes rather than about guestbook
114	  entries; the sentences themselves stay beside the endpoint that produces them, and only the
115	  envelope is shared. `app/platform/schemas/text.py` carries how a text field is normalized,
116	  trimmed and measured, which is a fact about EVERY text field this API accepts; the *bounds*
117	  stay where their domain is (`AUTHOR_MAX_LENGTH` beside the model) and only the unit they
118	  count in is shared. The test of whether a third file belongs here is the same both times: not
119	  "is it generic" but "is it a fact about every one of these, rather than about one context's". `app/core/` and `app/db/` are **not** under this name, because they are used by
120	  Platform and by every context alike and filing them under one slice would say something
121	  untrue about who they belong to.
122	- **`tests/<group>/test_<subject>.py`** — one of four groups, with no mirroring of the package
123	  tree inside any of them. `unit/` does not touch the database, `integration/` needs it,
124	  `fitness/` reads this repository's source as text, `tooling/` covers `scripts/` and the
125	  end-to-end harness. **The directory is a declaration**: each of the three database-free groups
126	  carries a `conftest.py` that applies `no_db` to everything below it, so the marker cannot be
127	  forgotten, and `tests/fitness/test_test_layout.py` proves the converse. Shared helpers stay
128	  flat as `tests/_<subject>.py`. Reference data in `golden-set/`, located by
129	  `tests/_golden_set.py`, and the repository root by `tests/_repo.py` — never by counting
130	  directories, which broke eleven modules at once the first time the suite was grouped.
131	  **`golden-set/` is itself two declarations**: `fixtures/` is what a suite reads and asserts
132	  about, `seed/` is what a new environment opens with — the same rule as the test groups, one
133	  directory up. See [`testing.md`](testing.md).
134	- **One exception, and only one**: the tests of the SDD framework itself live beside the code
135	  they prove, as the engine's own tests. Most of them read their subject's
136	  *source* — which module defines a constant, which imports `fcntl`, which counts directories to
137	  find the repository root — and a check that reads source belongs beside it. The same `pytest`
138	  run collects them (`testpaths` names both roots), so this is an exception of layout rather
139	  than a second suite. The application's tests stay flat under `tests/`; this exception does not
140	  generalise.
141	
142	**Placeholder columns stay unwritten**: a column whose owning feature has not landed is nullable
143	and no service writes it; the docstring names the blocking feature.
144	
145	## Frontend — where a file goes
146	
147	**Cut by context first, exactly as the backend is**, because a screen is owned by the context
148	whose rules it shows, and because the same argument about `.github/CODEOWNERS` applies on this
149	side of the wire. What is left at the top level is what genuinely belongs to no context.
150	
151	```
152	frontend/src/
153	  contexts/<name>/   pages components hooks lib — one context's screen and everything of it
154	  components/ui/     design-system primitives, no business logic
155	  components/shell/  the frame every screen renders itself inside
156	  hooks/  lib/       rules and helpers that are about no context in particular
157	  api/               the generated contract and the client over it
158	  router.tsx         the composition root: the one module that binds a path to a screen
159	  routes.ts          the route constants, shared by the shell, the 404 page and the screen
160	```
161	
162	- **`frontend/src/contexts/<name>/`** — one context's screen and everything only it uses:
163	  `pages/<Name>Page.tsx`, its `components/`, its `hooks/`, its `lib/`. A module here may not
164	  import another context's folder; `tests/fitness/test_context_boundaries.py` refuses it, and
165	  `router.tsx` is the one named exception because binding a path to a screen is what a
166	  composition root does.
167	- **`frontend/src/pages/`** — screens belonging to no context: today `StatusPages.tsx`, which
168	  is what a wrong address gets. A screen that shows a context's rules belongs in that context.
169	  **Route paths are English** (`/guestbook`), like everything else in this repository
170	  (§ Language), and they live in `frontend/src/routes.ts` — a route is the application's
171	  composition rather than a context's internals, which is why a shared layout component no
172	  longer owns one.
173	- **`frontend/src/components/ui/`** — design-system primitives, no business logic, no data
174	  fetching. Export the component **and** its props interface. **Encode intent in variants, not
175	  in callers**: the `red` variant of `Banner` means "this is a loss, not a warning", and that is
176	  why an irreversible message cannot accidentally be made to look like an ordinary one. **A
177	  primitive with no caller is removed**, not kept in reserve: a component nobody renders is a
178	  branch nobody reviews against a screen.
179	- **`frontend/src/hooks/`** — two kinds, both tied to React. One TanStack Query hook per resource
180	  (`use<Resource>.ts`, exporting a `<resource>Keys` object; **components never call `client.GET`
181	  directly**) and hooks for state in the URL — filters, sorting and paging live in the address,
182	  so a screen can be shared and survives a reload (`useEntryQueryParams.ts`). A parameter at its
183	  default value is **absent** from the address, and a write replaces the history entry rather
184	  than adding one. The *rules* those hooks apply live in `lib/`.
185	- **`frontend/src/lib/`** — pure rules and formatting that belong to no context, one concern
186	  per file, named after it (`datetime.ts`, `relativeTime.ts`, `number.ts`, `cn.ts`). A rule
187	  about one context's data lives in that context's `lib/`
188	  (`contexts/guestbook/lib/guestbookEntry.ts`, `contexts/guestbook/lib/entryListCopy.ts`,
189	  `contexts/guestbook/lib/entryText.ts`), and moves up here the day a second context needs it —
190	  never before, because a shared module with one caller is a boundary drawn in the wrong place.
191	  **Only the rule moves up.** A test that proves it through one context's bounds stays beside
192	  that context's modules and changes one import. The corpus reader
193	  `frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/lib/entryText.test.ts` is one such test. Moved up here, it
194	  would have to import a context's bound, and nothing here imports from `contexts/`.
195	  `entryText.ts` is the case worth naming: its Python counterpart sits in `app/platform/`
196	  because the server has more than one caller for it, and this one stays in the context because
197	  the browser has exactly one. The asymmetry is each tree following its own rule rather than an
198	  oversight in either.
199	
200	  Rejected (decision of 2026-09-17, `cr: historical` — where the two halves of the text rule go,
201	  decided on GitHub issue #28, outside `/forge:sdd`):
202	
203	  - **Put both in the context, and add no file to `app/platform/`.** It keeps the trees
204	    symmetrical and says something untrue: how this API trims and measures text is a fact about
205	    every text field it accepts, and the schemas and the service are already two callers. The
206	    next context would copy the rule rather than import it, which is how a shared fact becomes
207	    two facts.
208	  - **Put both above the contexts, in `app/platform/` and `frontend/src/lib/`.** Symmetrical the
209	    other way, and it breaks this section's own rule: a shared module with one caller is a
210	    boundary drawn in the wrong place, and the browser has exactly one caller today.
211	  - **Fold the rule into `guestbookEntry.ts` rather than giving it a file.** The search phrase is
212	    not an entry, and it is measured by the same rule — so the module would be named after one of
213	    its two subjects. Never `format.ts` or `utils.ts`. Nothing
214	  here imports from `components/` or from `contexts/` — both are dependency arrows pointing
215	  backwards.
216	- **`frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts`** — generated, never edited. Domain types are aliased from it
217	  (`type GuestbookEntry = components['schemas']['GuestbookEntryRead']`). Regenerate rather than
218	  widen.
219	- **`frontend/src/styles/theme.css`** — the application's colour tokens and the only place where
220	  colour and typeface are written down. Everything that is neither — sizes, spacing, radii,
221	  shadows — comes from the Tailwind scale. A token name may not collide with a class name from
222	  that scale (`spec/design/ui/system-states.md` § One palette). **Never a raw hex value or a
223	  bracketed value in a component** — a raw colour is a token nobody has named yet, and it is
224	  invisible to every later change of the palette.
225	
226	**Frontend tests** are `vitest`, `*.test.ts(x)` placed beside the module they test. The weight is
227	carried by the pure rules in `lib/` and the generated-contract adapters in `api/`; a component
228	test that asserts only that it rendered is noise.
229	
230	Screens are specified before they are built, one document per screen under [`ui/`](ui/) — that
231	rule, and the reason Markdown beats a mock-up, are given by [`ui/README.md`](ui/README.md).
232	
233	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-07, `cr: historical` — the placement rule changed from
234	layer-first to context-first, and this document is where placement rules live; the recut was
235	done on the trunk and carries no `delta.md` in which to declare the edit. What the system is
236	now made of, and the alternatives weighed there:
237	[`architecture.md`](architecture.md) § What a new feature adds):
238	
239	- **Leave placement alone.** The layer-first tree broke no rule in this document and produced
240	  no defect. It made exactly one thing impossible, and the thing is the reason for the change:
241	  a path that holds one context. Ownership is what sdd107 puts before hierarchy and before any
242	  automation, and a rule nobody can be given is a rule with no addressee.
243	- **Say the rule and move the files later.** A placement rule describing a tree that does not
244	  exist is the failure `docs/` is forbidden from having: a document read as normative that
245	  nothing holds. The fitness functions in `tests/fitness/test_context_boundaries.py` are what
246	  make this rule real, and they cannot be written against an absent shape.
247	- **Let a context's `lib/`, `hooks/` and `components/` stay shared and cut only the pages.**
248	  Half a boundary. The screen would move and the rules behind it would not, so two contexts
249	  would still meet in `frontend/src/lib/`, which is where the collision actually is.
250	
251	## Boundaries — where a contract goes
252	
253	A boundary is where the system meets something it does not compile together with itself. At a
254	boundary the contract is the authority and the code is validated against it (constitution,
255	article VI; the decision and its rejected alternatives:
256	[`contracts/README.md`](../../contracts/README.md)).
257	
258	- **`contracts/<kind>/<area>.yaml|.md`** — one file per area, named after the area, **written by
259	  hand and committed**. `openapi/` for HTTP, `asyncapi/` for events, `invariants/` for data
260	  invariants. Every subdirectory carries a `README.md` with a declared compatibility mode; a
261	  directory with no contract declares `**Status:** empty starter` in it, because silence and a
262	  decision look identical in a file tree.
263	- **Never generate a file into this directory.** A copy of a dump has no authority over what it
264	  was copied from; `contracts` (`G20` until the rename) refuses a file with a generator banner, and one shell redirection is
265	  the whole way back to the state this decision reversed.
266	- **The database schema is not here, and that is a decision.** The set of revisions in
267	  `alembic/versions/` is its contract ([`data-model.md`](data-model.md) § Owner of the schema);
268	  the compatibility mode is declared beside the schema, in the same document.
269	- **A machine's output stays output.** `openapi.json` is gitignored and rebuilt on every run;
270	  `./scripts/contracts.sh` compares it against the contract.
271	
272	## Documentation — where a document goes
273	
274	A document that is not normative still has one home, and which home decides who it is written
275	for. Three trees, three readers, and the cut is by **subject** rather than by tone:
276	
277	| Tree | Subject | Reader |
278	|---|---|---|
279	| [`docs/`](../../docs/README.md) | the system: how to set it up, run it, configure it, watch it, back it up and repair it | whoever operates or takes delivery of the application |
280	| [the marketplace's README](https://github.com/Scalo-Sales-Engineering-Consulting/claude-marketplace/blob/main/README.md), and the orchestrator's own document ([`skills/sdd/SKILL.md`](https://github.com/Scalo-Sales-Engineering-Consulting/claude-marketplace/blob/main/plugins/forge/skills/sdd/SKILL.md)) | the change process: how a change travels, and the decision table that drives it | whoever runs, ports or alters the process |
281	| [`../rationale/`](../rationale/README.md) | reasoning worth keeping that is not a decision — why a shape was chosen, what was tried, how it broke | whoever changes this in six months |
282	
283	Four rules hold over `docs/`, and each exists because its absence has a named cost:
284	
285	- **Nothing in `docs/` binds.** Where a rule holds, it holds because it stands in `spec/` or
286	  `contracts/`, and the document here **cites the one that owns it**. A descriptive document
287	  read as normative is a second home for one rule, which is the failure
288	  [`../README.md`](../README.md) exists to prevent. Every document therefore carries a
289	  `**For:**` line naming its reader and a `**Normative source:**` line naming what it defers to.
290	- **One subject per file, named after the subject.** `configuration.md`, `monitoring.md` — never
291	  `misc.md`, never a number in the filename. The same rule as § Naming, for the same reason: a
292	  directory that numbers its documents has stopped being able to say what is in them.
293	- **A procedure is a runbook and lives in `docs/runbooks/`.** A runbook says when to use it, the
294	  steps in order, and how you know it worked. A procedure with no last section cannot be
295	  finished by the person who did not write it, which is the person who reads it at three in the
296	  morning.
297	- **Every instruction invokes a script** (the constitution, article XII). A document that tells
298	  somebody to type `terraform apply` has taught them to skip the guard, and the guard is the
299	  point of `scripts/`. The named exception is the AWS CLI, which genuinely is the interface for
300	  the few steps no script wraps.
301	
302	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-06, `cr: historical` — the process manual and the system's
303	documentation were both in `docs/`, and only one of them was there; framework changes are made
304	on the trunk and carry no `delta.md` in which to declare the edit):
305	
306	- **Leave the process manual in `docs/` and give the system's documentation another directory.**
307	  It puts the tree a client reads one directory away from the tree explaining an agent
308	  framework, and names the visitor's directory after the resident. `docs/` is the first place
309	  anybody looks for a manual to the thing the repository builds.
310	- **One directory, two subjects, separated by a naming prefix.** The prefix is a convention a
311	  reader has to learn before the index is legible, and nothing enforces it. The directory
312	  boundary is enforced by the file system.
313	- **Leave `docs/` unwritten and let the operational facts stay where they are** — in
314	  `infra/README.md`, in `CLAUDE.md`, in script headers and in module docstrings. That was the
315	  state this replaces, and its cost is measurable: the rollback semantics lived only in
316	  `scripts/deploy.sh --help`, the log-level convention only in a Python docstring, and no
317	  document anywhere named a restore procedure. Facts that live only where they were written are
318	  facts only their author can find.
319	
320	## Language
321	
322	**The whole repository is written in English.** Prose, identifiers, file names and
323	directory names; `spec/` and `contracts/` along with everything else; the interface, the
324	route paths, the refusal sentences the backend produces, the Gherkin scenarios, the SDD
325	process layer and the scripts. Gate `english` enforces it, and it enforces both halves: the
326	sentences inside a file are judged by counting, and the name of the file is judged by
327	looking it up, because a path has no function words to count.
328	
329	**A number in prose takes a comma as its thousands separator** — `10,000`, never `10 000`.
330	The spaced form is Polish typography that survived the translation in one document while its
331	neighbours used the comma, and a reader should not have to know the repository's history to
332	read a number.
333	
334	**This reverses the decision of 2026-08-31**, which is recorded here rather than deleted.
335	That decision drew the line where a person starts reading a screen: interface copy became
336	English, while route paths, backend refusal sentences, the Gherkin suite and the whole of
337	`spec/` and `contracts/` stayed Polish. Its reasoning was sound at the time — the guestbook
338	screen was rebuilt from a Claude Design mock-up whose sentences are *content*, the routes
339	were already written down and linked, and refusal sentences are backend text that reaches
340	every client rather than one screen. What it produced was a repository with a seam through
341	it: two languages, and a rule for which side of the seam each artefact falls on. The
342	option this reverses to was named and rejected on that day as "English everywhere, routes
343	and refusals included"; the cost it was rejected for — broken links and backend text moving
344	during a frontend change — is a one-off cost that gets larger every month it is deferred,
345	while the seam is a cost paid at every reading.
346	
347	**Rejected, again and for the same reasons as before:** a bilingual tree with translation
348	files (it solves a problem this product does not have and adds a second place for copy to
349	drift from the screen specification — it comes back with a second audience and its own
350	decision); and keeping historical documents in the language they were written in (an audit
351	nobody can read is not a record, and `spec/rationale/` exists to be read). Introducing i18n
352	later still does not require undoing this: English becomes one of the languages, rather
353	than a layer to take off.
354	
355	**What is not translated, and why.** These are not exceptions to the rule; they are things
356	the rule was never about.
357	
358	| What | Stays as it is |
359	|---|---|
360	| parsed keywords — EARS `WHEN`/`SHALL`, delta labels `ADDED`/`MODIFIED`/`REMOVED`, the `**ADR:** none` and `**Verified-by:** manual` markers, front-matter status values | already English, and a contract rather than prose |
361	| stable refusal codes (`guestbook_entry_not_found`) | a contract surface: the code is what a client matches on, and rewording it is a breaking change |
362	| the credential names `e2e/harness/client.py` redacts | a denylist, not prose — dropping a spelling narrows what gets redacted |
363	| non-ASCII text in `golden-set/` | evidence that bytes survive the round trip. **Each half** must carry characters above U+007F; neither need carry any particular language |
364	| a quoted Polish phrase, a proper noun, a historical file name | quotation. `english` has a floor of five lines so that quoting does not read as writing |
365	| `spec/rationale/mockup-guestbook/support.js` | vendored runtime of a design tool, not authored here |
366	
367	**Domain terms keep their source form inside identifiers** (`GuestbookEntry`, `author`), so
368	a field can be grepped from the specification down to the column — see
369	[`../glossary.md`](../glossary.md).
370	
371	## Naming
372	
373	- **Python files and functions**: `snake_case`. Private helpers prefixed with `_`
374	  (`_normalize_iban`), kept in the module that uses them.
375	- **Python model files**: singular (`models/guestbook_entry.py`); schema, service and router
376	  files plural (`schemas/guestbook_entries.py`) — a model is one thing, an API is a collection.
377	- **TS components and files**: `PascalCase.tsx` matching the exported component. **Hooks**:
378	  `useThing.ts`; **libraries**: `camelCase.ts` (`lib/guestbookEntry.ts`).
379	- **Domain field names**: exactly as the source specification names them (`author`, `message`,
380	  `created_at`), so that a field can be grepped from the specification to the column.
381	
382	### A gate is named, not numbered
383	
384	A gate's identifier is the name of what it checks: `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`, lower case, hyphens,
385	**no slash and no dot**. The register is
386	[the engine's `spec_gates.py`](https://github.com/Scalo-Sales-Engineering-Consulting/claude-marketplace/blob/main/plugins/forge/skills/_shared/sdd/spec_gates.py),
387	and it is the source the two documentation tables and the exemptable list are all compared
388	against.
389	
390	The shape rule is not aesthetic. `backtick-paths` and `source-paths` read every backticked
391	token containing a slash as a repository path and check that it exists, so a gate called
392	`spec/links` would make every document that names it fail two other gates — and the failure
393	would be reported against the document rather than against the name. `test_sdd_spec_lint.py`
394	asserts the shape rather than trusting this sentence.
395	
396	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-06, `cr: historical` — the gates were renamed from `G1`…`G20` to
397	descriptive names; this document is where naming rules live, and framework changes are made on
398	the trunk, so there is no `delta.md` in which to declare the edit):
399	
400	- **Keep the numbers.** `G12` says nothing about what it checks, so every mention costs a
401	  reader a lookup in a table two directories away. Twenty of them, in three modules, two
402	  documentation tables and six regexes — and the audits under `spec/rationale/` are a record
403	  of that cost being paid.
404	- **Rename and renumber, closing the holes.** `G9` and `G13` are withdrawn, and renumbering
405	  would tidy the sequence by destroying the one thing a hole carries
406	  ([`../invariants.md`](../invariants.md)).
407	- **Keep both, a name beside a code.** Two homes for one fact, which this repository refuses
408	  everywhere else, and the second home is the one that goes stale.
409	- **Split `G4` or leave it whole.** It covered three unrelated rules — EARS discipline, a delta
410	  entry's `**Why:**`, and task shape — so a single name for it would have been vague where the
411	  three checks are precise, an exemption row naming it silenced all three, and a CI annotation
412	  titled with it named none of them. Split into `requirements`, `delta-entries` and `tasks`.
413	
414	Consequences: `G9` and `G13` stay withdrawn and gain no name, because a name for a rule nobody
415	raises is an invitation to write an exemption for it. The old codes are neither reused nor
416	erased — `spec/rationale/` and `retro/` keep them verbatim, and
417	[the process's `spec_gates.py`](https://github.com/Scalo-Sales-Engineering-Consulting/claude-marketplace/blob/main/plugins/forge/skills/_shared/sdd/spec_gates.py) maps every
418	one to the name it became. The count went from eighteen to twenty on the day of the rename, and
419	stands at twenty-two now (`operations-doc` and `documentation-set` came afterwards). Enforced by
420	`test_sdd_spec_lint.py`, which compares the register against both documentation tables — names,
421	order, family and exemptability — and by `test_sdd_spec_summary.py`, which compares the rows the
422	job summary prints against the gates the code actually raises.
423	
424	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-10, `cr: historical` — the forge plugin deleted its `docs/` tree
425	on 2026-09-10: the handbook, the reference and their index exist nowhere, so the documentation
426	table above names what the process still has — the marketplace's README for a person, the
427	orchestrator's own document for the table that drives a change — and the mapping from a retired
428	gate code to its name is read off `spec_gates.py`, the register where every gate declares the code
429	it carried. Framework changes are made on the trunk and carry no `delta.md`): keeping links that
430	return 404, or vendoring a copy of the deleted pages here — the second home this section argues
431	against.
432	
433	## Type safety
434	
435	- **Backend**: full annotations, `Mapped[...]` on every column. Optionality expressed in the
436	  type (`str | None`), not only in the column arguments. `mypy --strict` covers `app`,
437	  `scripts`, `e2e`, `.claude/skills`, `tests/unit` and `tests/fitness`.
438	- **Frontend**: `tsc --noEmit` is part of `build`. API types come from the generated
439	  `src/api/schema.d.ts` — regenerate rather than widen a type.
440	- **The syntax floor is lower than the runtime floor, and deliberately.** `pyproject.toml` pins
441	  `requires-python` to what the application runs on, and `ruff`'s `target-version` to what the
442	  code may be *written* in; the second is the older of the two. The bare-machine scripts start
443	  on whatever `python3` a machine has on PATH rather than on the interpreter `uv` provisions —
444	  `scripts/preflight.py` reporting what is missing, `scripts/ci_summary.py` in the aggregate CI
445	  job, `scripts/app_status.py` behind `status.sh` — and a script that reports a missing Python
446	  cannot ask for one before it parses. `tests/fitness/test_scripts_syntax_floor.py` parses them
447	  at that floor and holds `target-version` to it. The change process holds its own hooks to the
448	  same floor in its own suite, with a `target-version` of its own.
449	
450	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-08, `cr: historical` — the project moved to Python 3.14 and the
451	first `ruff format` under `target-version = "py314"` rewrote `except (A, B):` into the PEP 758
452	form across the framework, which every older interpreter refuses with a SyntaxError; found the
453	same day, on the trunk, where there is no `delta.md` to declare the edit in):
454	
455	- **Raise `target-version` with the runtime and mark the two entry points `# fmt: skip`.** One
456	  number instead of two, and it holds exactly until somebody adds a third module to the hooks'
457	  import closure without knowing the marker exists. What it buys is a SyntaxError raised before
458	  any of this project's own error handling runs, on a contributor's machine rather than in CI.
459	- **Require Python 3.14 on PATH.** Nothing can enforce it: the check that would say so is written
460	  in the syntax that fails to parse.
461	
462	## Imports
463	
464	Static, named imports only — no star imports. First-party imports in the backend are always
465	absolute, from `app.`; no relative imports between packages. The frontend uses the `@/` alias
466	for anything outside the current feature folder, and relative paths inside it.
467	
468	```python
469	import datetime                      # standard library
470	from sqlalchemy import select        # third party
471	from app.contexts.guestbook.models.guestbook_entry import GuestbookEntry   # first party, absolute from `app.`
472	```
473	
474	```typescript
475	import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'  // third party
476	import { client } from '@/api/client'             // absolute, outside this feature
477	import { EntryRow } from './EntryRow'             // relative, same feature
478	```
479	
480	**One exception, mechanical rather than stylistic**: `e2e/suite/test_scenarios.py` star-imports
481	the step modules. A pytest-bdd step definition is not a decorated function — the decorator
482	writes a *fixture* into its defining module's globals under a generated name, and pytest sees
483	fixtures only in the module it collects, so a named import registers nothing. The two routes on
484	which this can break silently (an `__all__` in a step module, a step module nobody imports) are
485	both checked by `tests/fitness/test_e2e_scenarios.py`.
486	
487	## After a change
488	
489	- **After an API change**: `./scripts/generate.sh`, then commit what it changed.
490	  `frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts` is committed and CI regenerates and compares it;
491	  `openapi.json` itself is gitignored, because an intermediate product must never go stale in
492	  git.
493	- **Every task is one `.sh` script** over the shared `_lib.sh`; task scripts written in Python
494	  are libraries that the `.sh` calls, not a second entry point to the task. The scripts are
495	  POSIX (§ Scripts).
496	
497	## Scripts
498	
499	**Every task is one `.sh` script over the shared `_lib.sh`, and Windows is not a runtime
500	platform of this project** — it is supported through WSL or Git Bash and through nothing else.
501	This is a named absence of support, not an oversight (decision of 2026-08-31).
502	
503	The history without which this rule looks like convenience: article XII once demanded every
504	task as a `.sh` **and** a `.ps1`, and one rule had six mechanisms holding it — gate `G13` (the
505	twins change in one diff), three loops in `hygiene.sh`, three CI steps, a `windows-latest` leg,
506	a 309-line fitness function reading PowerShell as text, and a module choosing the dialect.
507	Despite them the twins kept diverging: `test.ps1` read a variable it never defined, `start.ps1`
508	lost `--development`, `_lib.ps1` hard-coded the port. **A second copy of the same logic diverges
509	faster than the checks can detect it**, and the PowerShell half was written without any way of
510	running it even once, because `pwsh` was on no developer machine.
511	
512	Rejected: keeping the twins (the status quo, at the price above); a `windows-latest` leg running
513	the `.sh` through Git Bash (no Linux Docker, no executable bit on NTFS, a different `PATH`
514	separator — a leg failing on the harness rather than on the subject of the test); generating the
515	`.ps1` from the `.sh` (a third artefact that returns to hand editing on the first script outside
516	the generator's grammar).
517	
518	Consequences: `G13` is **withdrawn, not free** — the number in an archived change record still
519	means what it meant ([`../invariants.md`](../invariants.md)); the Python branches whose only
520	reason was Windows are gone; `check.sh` no longer fails to reproduce just one CI leg, and that
521	leg is macOS. This is enforced by `scripts/hygiene.sh` and the `scripts` job in CI (a loop over
522	`scripts/*.sh`: the executable bit, presence in `help.sh`, an answer to `--help`) and by
523	`test_sdd_paths.py::test_no_module_decides_what_platform_this_is`.
524	
525	**`scripts/` is the application's interface and never calls the change process.** The process
526	has commands of its own — `sdd-specs`, `sdd-verify`, `sdd-retro`, `sdd-tests`,
527	`sdd-lint`, `sdd-preview-mock` — over a library of its own that sources nothing from here, and
528	what the process may call in `scripts/` is the script contract
529	([`script-contract.md`](https://github.com/Scalo-Sales-Engineering-Consulting/claude-marketplace/blob/main/plugins/forge/docs/script-contract.md)): `check`, `test`,
530	`setup` and the lifecycle scripts, by the names `.specconf/stack.json` declares. A script here
531	that reached into the process's own tree would be the one dependency in the direction the split forbids -- and since 2026-09-09 there is no such tree here to reach into.
532	
533	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-09, `cr: historical` — the process became independent of the
534	application it works on, so that one process serves many templates; framework changes are made
535	on the trunk and carry no `delta.md`): keeping the process's five scripts (`specs.sh`,
536	`verify.sh`, `retro.sh`, `sdd-tests.sh`, `preview-mock.sh`) in this directory. They put the
537	process's gates into `check.sh`, its tests into this project's `pytest` and its verdicts into
538	this project's CI, and a template that wanted a different process would have had to edit five of
539	its own scripts to get one.
540	
541	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-09, `cr: historical` — the seam above was cut in this repository
542	and the process still lived in it; on the same day it moved out entirely, into the plugin
543	`forge@scalo`. Every link here that reached it by a relative path
544	(`../../.claude/docs/…`, `../../.claude/skills/_shared/sdd/…`) named a path that exists in no
545	clone of this template, so each one is now either the URL of the document in the repository
546	that ships it, or the name of a command that arrives on PATH with the plugin. Framework
547	changes are made on the trunk and carry no `delta.md`): vendoring the process's documents into
548	`docs/` so the links could stay relative. That is the second home this section exists to
549	forbid, and it would go stale the first time the process changed without this template.
550	
551	## When a decision is an ADR
552	
553	The classic threshold — "an architectural decision with a rejected alternative" — is too low and
554	lets almost everything through, because choosing a column name also rejects an alternative. The
555	effect was observed: the directory swells, ADRs duplicate normative documents, and a question
556	arises that cannot be settled — does a rule hold because `spec/design/` says so, or because an
557	ADR says so.
558	
559	**An ADR is written only when a decision meets BOTH conditions:** it is **cross-cutting**
560	(reversing it touches more than one module, one layer or one suite) and it is **expensive to
561	reverse** (undoing it needs a data migration, a rewritten contract or a change in CI, not an
562	edit to one file). A rejected alternative is necessary and **not sufficient**. A decision that
563	fails either condition has an address, and it is not `spec/ADR/`:
564	
565	| Kind of ruling | Home |
566	|---|---|
567	| A fact always true of the data | `contracts/invariants/` |
568	| A deliberate non-goal | [`../invariants.md`](../invariants.md) |
569	| Where a file goes, what it is called, what it imports | this document |
570	| The choice of a suite, a fixture or a marker | [`testing.md`](testing.md) |
571	| A column, a type, a constraint | [`data-model.md`](data-model.md) |
572	| A contract field, a refusal code | [`api.md`](api.md) |
573	| A business rule or a flow | `spec/contexts/<context>.md` |
574	
575	**An ADR is never edited after acceptance.** A later ADR supersedes it, with `supersedes`.
576	Rewriting a decision in place destroys the reasoning behind it, and then nobody can tell a
577	settled decision from an accident. Rejected: a lower threshold (it produces a directory in which
578	a rule has two homes); no ADRs at all (normative documents say what holds **now**, without a
579	date and without a rejected alternative — and that is the knowledge whose absence makes somebody
580	take the same lost decision again two years later); an ADR editable in place (after a year it
581	says what somebody thinks today, not what was decided then).
582	
583	**The state of `spec/ADR/`: empty, until the first change carried out through `/sdd`.** Eleven
584	decisions taken between 2026-08-30 and 2026-09-02 without a change record (`cr: historical`)
585	were written on 2026-09-02 into the normative documents they concern — with a date, a reason and
586	the rejected alternatives, where the rule stands — because an ADR with no parent in
587	`spec/changes/` has no history to point back to, and two homes for one rule are the failure
588	described above. Every future ADR comes out of a change record (`design-adr` writes the draft,
589	`reconcile-design` gives it a number) and carries that change's `cr:`; the index
590	`spec/ADR/index.md` is generated by `gen_indexes.py`, and gate `frozen-ids` holds that a cited
591	`ADR-NNNN` exists.
592	
593	**A decision taken on the trunk is written into the document whose rule it changes**, in the
594	shape those eleven used, and gate `recorded-decision` reads it:
595	
596	```
597	Rejected (decision of <YYYY-MM-DD>, `cr: historical` — <why this was taken outside /sdd>):
598	
599	- **The alternative** — and the reason it was not taken.
600	```
601	
602	The date, the marker and a reason are all required. `cr: historical` on its own is a label on
603	the fact that no ADR was written rather than an answer, which is the same bar
604	`**ADR:** none — <reason>` has to clear in a `delta.md`.
605	
606	The gate takes this answer **only from a diff that carries no change directory**. Inside `/sdd`
607	the duty is unchanged — `design-adr` writes the ADR, or the delta says why the edit was
608	editorial — because an exit available to a change that merely felt like typing it is a way round
609	both. It reads what the diff **added**, and it asks it of **each** rule document that moved: a
610	decision covers the edit it was written for, not every later edit of the same file, and a
611	decision recorded in one document says nothing about a rule that moved in another.
612	
613	So a decision has four homes, and which one it gets is decided by where the work is done rather
614	than by preference:
615	
616	| Where the work is | What records the decision |
617	|---|---|
618	| A change, and the decision is cross-cutting and expensive to reverse | an ADR under `spec/ADR/` |
619	| A change, and the edit carries no decision | `**ADR:** none — <reason>` in that change's `delta.md` |
620	| The trunk, and the decision is real | the block above, in the document it changes |
621	| Anything else | a dated row in [`../changes/EXEMPTIONS.md`](../changes/EXEMPTIONS.md), which expires |
622	
623	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-05, `cr: historical` — this taught `G5` its third answer, and the
624	gate is the change process rather than the product, so it is recorded here):
625	
626	- **Leave `G5` as it was.** It had three doors and, from the trunk, no key: both of its exits
627	  live inside a change directory, and the paragraph above forbids the ADR outright. The work it
628	  blocks is not hypothetical — `contracts/` and the golden-set split were both done this way —
629	  and it was invisible only because `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs the diff-scoped gates on a
630	  pull request alone. A gate that holds because nothing runs it has been deleted without anyone
631	  saying so.
632	- **Send trunk edits through the `spec-exempt` label and a dated row.** It calls a satisfied duty
633	  an exception. The decision is recorded, in the place this section prescribes; a row would say
634	  the opposite in the register, expire on a morning when nobody committed anything, and silence
635	  eight diff-scoped gates in order to silence one — and `EXEMPTIONS.md` reserves rows for work
636	  stretched across several changes.
637	- **Write the ADR anyway.** It has no parent in `spec/changes/` to point back to, and it gives
638	  the rule the second home the whole section exists to prevent.
639	- **Match the block against the file on disk.** `architecture.md` already holds one. Read that
640	  way it would have exempted every future edit of the most-edited rule document in the tree, for
641	  ever, on the strength of a decision taken in September 2026.
642	- **Take one block anywhere in the diff, as the ADR exit does.** An ADR is a document about a
643	  decision and stands on its own; this block is a paragraph inside the rule it justifies, and
644	  its whole value is that the reason sits where the rule sits.
645	
646	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-10, `cr: historical` — the marketplace moved organisation
647	and was renamed `scalo` there. Both halves of the citation had to move with it:
648	the absolute links, which named the organisation this repository was forked out of, and the
649	install id, because the marketplace's name is what an install resolves by. Framework changes
650	are made on the trunk and carry no `delta.md`): changing only the URLs and leaving the previous
651	install id standing in the prose. The id is the argument `claude plugin install` takes, so a
652	rule document that still names the retired one hands the next reader a command that fails, and
653	does it in the document that decides where a fact is allowed to live.
654
